title: The Rooftop Garden
passage:
When the heat finally softened one October evening, Huda carried three clay pots up to the flat roof of her family's building in Jeddah. Her grandfather had promised that mint, basil and a small lemon tree could survive there if she was patient enough to water them before sunrise.

For two weeks nothing happened, and Huda began to wonder whether the seeds had simply given up. Then, on a windy Friday morning, a ring of tiny green leaves pushed through the soil like a crowd of curious neighbours. "What a wonderful surprise!" she whispered, kneeling beside the pots.

By winter the roof smelled of mint tea and wet earth. Her grandfather admitted that the garden had grown faster than his own had, many years before, because Huda had recorded every watering in a small notebook.

questions.stem: Which word from the story is a noun?
questions.why: A garden is a thing, so it is a noun.

questions.stem: Which sentence from the story is exclamatory?
options: By winter the roof smelled of mint tea.
questions.why: It shows strong feeling and ends with an exclamation mark.

questions.stem: Why did Huda water the pots before sunrise?
options: Her grandfather told her the plants needed it then.
The pots were too heavy at noon.
questions.why: Her grandfather promised the plants could survive if she watered them before sunrise.

questions.stem: What happened right after Huda began to wonder whether the seeds had given up?
options: Tiny leaves pushed through the soil.
questions.why: The next event in the story is the ring of tiny green leaves appearing.

questions.stem: What caused Huda's garden to grow faster than her grandfather's had?
options: She recorded every watering in a notebook.
questions.why: The last paragraph links the fast growth to her careful notebook.

questions.stem: What does the phrase "like a crowd of curious neighbours" show about the leaves?
options: They seemed to be eagerly peeking out together.
questions.why: The simile pictures many small leaves appearing together as if looking around.

questions.stem: Which opinion is best supported by the story?
options: Gardening on a roof is impossible.
Patience and careful habits help living things grow.
questions.why: Huda's patience and notebook led to success.

questions.stem: Which information in the story is the least clear?
options: How the lemon tree grew by winter
The month she carried the pots
Who promised the plants could survive
questions.why: The story never says what happened to the lemon tree.

questions.stem: Which event in the story could really happen?
options: Mint grows in a pot on a roof in winter.
The lemon tree walks to the shade.
Seeds give up and leave the pots.
questions.why: Mint can really grow in a pot; the other events are imaginary.

questions.stem: Which is the best alternative title for the story?
questions.why: It names the main character and the main event.
